(2) an initial medical examination and follow-up referral or treatment, without charge, for youth during their participation in such activity;

(3) at least one nutritious meal daily, without charge, for participating youth during each day of participation;

(4) high quality instruction in a variety of sports (that shall include swimming and that may include dance and any other high quality recreational activity) provided by coaches and teachers from institutions of higher education and from elementary and secondary schools (as defined in section 7801 of title 20); and

(5) enrichment instruction and information on matters relating to the well-being of youth, to include educational opportunities and information on study practices, education for the prevention of drug and alcohol abuse, and information on health and nutrition, career opportunities, and family and job responsibilities.


(c) Advisory committee; partnerships The eligible service provider shall, in each community in which a program is funded under this section—

(1) ensure that—

(A) a community-based advisory committee is established, with representatives from local youth, family, and social service organizations, schools, entities providing park and recreation services, and other community-based organizations serving high-risk youth; or

(B) an existing community-based advisory board, commission, or committee with similar membership is utilized to serve as the committee described in subparagraph (A); and


(2) enter into formal partnerships with youth-serving organizations or other appropriate social service entities in order to link program participants with year-round services in their home communities that support and continue the objectives of this chapter.


(d) Eligible providers A service provider that is a national private, nonprofit organization, a coalition of such organizations, or a private, nonprofit organization applying jointly with a business concern shall be eligible to apply for a grant under this section if—

(1) the applicant has demonstrated experience in operating a program providing instruction to low-income youth;

(2) the applicant agrees to contribute an amount (in cash or in kind, fairly evaluated) of not less than 25 percent of the amount requested, for the program funded through the grant;

(3) the applicant agrees to use no funds from a grant authorized under this section for administrative expenses; and

(4) the applicant agrees to comply with the regulations or program guidelines promulgated by the Secretary for use of funds made available through the grant.


(e) Application process

To be eligible to receive a grant under this section, a service provider shall submit to the Secretary, for approval, an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require.


(f) Promulgation of regulations or program guidelines

The Secretary shall promulgate regulations or program guidelines to ensure funds made available through a grant made under this section are used in accordance with the objectives of this chapter.


(g) Authorization of appropriations

There are authorized to be appropriated $15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 1999 through 2003 for grants to carry out this section.

§ 9925. Demonstration partnership agreements addressing needs of poor

(a) General authority

(1) In order to stimulate the development of new approaches to provide for greater self-sufficiency of the poor, to test and evaluate such new approaches, to disseminate project results and evaluation findings so that such approaches can be replicated, and to strengthen the integration, coordination, and redirection of activities to promote maximum self-sufficiency among the poor, the Secretary may make grants from funds appropriated under subsection (e) to eligible entities for the development and implementation of new and innovative approaches to deal with particularly critical needs or problems of the poor which are common to a number of communities. Grants may be made only with respect to applications which—

(A) involve activities which can be incorporated into or be closely coordinated with eligible entities’ ongoing programs;

(B) involve significant new combinations of resources or new and innovative approaches involving partnership agreements;

(C) are structured in a way that will, within the limits of the type of assistance or activities contemplated, most fully and effectively promote the purposes of the Community Services Block Grant Act [42 U.S.C. 9901 et seq.]; and

(D) contain an assurance that the applicant for such grants will obtain an independent, methodologically sound evaluation of the effectiveness of the activities carried out with such grant and will submit such evaluation to the Secretary.


(2) No grant may be made under this section unless an application is submitted to the Secretary at such time, in such manner, and containing or accompanied by such information, as the Secretary may require.

(3) Initial and subsequent grant awards may fully fund projects for periods of up to 3 years.


(b) Federal share; limitations

(1)

(A) Subject to subparagraph (B), grants awarded pursuant to this section shall be used for programs and shall not exceed 50 per centum of the cost of such programs.

(B) After the first funding period for which an eligible entity receives a grant under this section to carry out a program, the amount of a subsequent grant made under this section to such entity to carry out such program may not exceed 80 percent of the amount of the grant previously received by such entity under this section to carry out such program.


(2) Non-Federal contributions may be in cash or in kind, fairly evaluated, including but not limited to plant, equipment, or services.

(3) Not more than one grant in each fiscal year may be made to any eligible entity, and no grant may exceed $350,000. Not more than 2 grants may be made under this section to an eligible entity to carry out a particular program.

(4) No application may be approved for assistance under this section unless the Secretary is satisfied that—

(A) the activities to be carried out under the application will be in addition to, and not in substitution for, activities previously carried on without Federal assistance; and

(B) funds or other resources devoted to programs designed to meet the needs of the poor within the community, area, or State will not be diminished in order to provide the matching contributions required under this section.



(c) Programs directed to special populations

(1) In addition to the grant programs described in subsection (a), the Secretary may make grants to community action agencies for the purpose of enabling such agencies to demonstrate new approaches to dealing with the problems caused by entrenched, chronic unemployment and lack of economic opportunities for urban youth. Demonstrations shall include such activities as peer counseling, mentoring, development of job skills, assistance with social skills, community services, family literacy, parenting skills, opportunities for employment or entrepreneurship, and other services designed to assist such at-risk youth to continue their education, to secure meaningful employment, to perform community service, or to pursue other productive alternatives within the community.

(2) Such grants may be made only with respect to applications that—

(A) identify and describe the population to be served, the problems to be addressed, the overall approach and methods of outreach and recruitment to be used, and the services to be provided;

(B) describe how the approach to be used differs from other approaches used for the population to be served by the project;

(C) describe the objectives of the project and contain a plan for measuring progress toward meeting those objectives; and

(D) contain assurances that the grantee will report on the progress and results of the demonstration at such times and in such manner as the Secretary shall require.


(3) Notwithstanding subsection (b), such grants shall not exceed 80 percent of the cost of such programs.

(4) Such grants made under this subsection on a competitive basis shall be based on an annual competition determined by the Secretary. Grants made under this subsection shall not exceed $500,000.


(d) Dissemination of results

As soon as practicable, but not later than 180 days after the end of the fiscal year in which a recipient of a grant under this section completes the expenditure of such grant, the Secretary shall prepare and make available to each State and each eligible entity a description of the program carried out with such grant, any relevant information developed and results achieved, and a summary of the evaluation of such program received under subsection (a)(1)(D) so as to provide a model of innovative programs for other eligible entities.


(e) Replication of programs

(1) The Secretary shall annually identify programs that receive grants under this section that demonstrate a significant potential for dealing with particularly critical needs or problems of the poor that exist in a number of communities.

(2) Not less than 10 percent, and not more than 25 percent, of the funds appropriated for each fiscal year to carry out this section shall be available to make grants under this section to replicate in additional geographic areas programs identified under paragraph (1).


(f) Omitted

(g) Definitions As used in this section—

(1) the term “eligible entity” has the same meaning given such term by section 673(1) of the Community Services Block Grant Act (42 U.S.C. 9902(1)), except that such term includes an organization that serves migrant and seasonal farm workers and that receives a grant under the Community Services Block Grant Act (42 U.S.C. 9901 et seq.) in the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year for which such organization requests a grant under this section; and

(2) the term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.


(h) Authorization of appropriations

(1) There are authorized to be appropriated $30,000,000 for fiscal year 1995, and such sums as may be necessary for fiscal years 1996, 1997, and 1998, to carry out this section.

(2) Of the amounts appropriated for this section, not less than 30 percent and not more than 40 percent shall be used to carry out the programs authorized under subsection (c).

(3) In addition to sums which are required to carry out the evaluation, reporting, and dissemination of results under subsections (a), (c), (d), and (f),1

1 See References in Text note below.

 the Secretary is authorized to reserve up to 2 percent of the amounts appropriated pursuant to subparagraphs (1) and (2) for administration of the program as well as for planning and technical assistance.

§ 9926. Projects to expand the number of job opportunities available to certain low-income individuals

(a) In general

The Secretary of Health and Human Services (in this section referred to as the “Secretary”) shall enter into agreements with nonprofit organizations (including community development corporations) submitting applications under this section for the purpose of conducting projects in accordance with subsection (b) to create employment opportunities for certain low-income individuals.


(b) Nature of project

(1) Each nonprofit organization conducting a project under this section shall provide technical and financial assistance to private employers in the community to assist them in creating employment and business opportunities for those individuals eligible to participate in the projects as described in this subsection.

(2) For purposes of this section, a nonprofit organization is any organization (including a community development corporation) exempt from taxation under section 501(a) of title 26 by reason of paragraph (3) or (4) of section 501(c) of such title.

(3) A low-income individual eligible to participate in a project conducted under this section is any individual eligible to receive assistance under the program funded part 1

1 So in original. Probably should be “under part”.

 A of title IV of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.] of the State in which the individual resides and any other individual whose income level does not exceed 100 percent of the official poverty line as defined by the Office of Management and Budget and revised in accordance with section 9902(2) of this title.


(c) Content of applications; selection priority

(1) Each nonprofit organization submitting an application under this section shall, as part of such application, describe—

(A) the technical and financial assistance that will be made available under the project conducted under this section;

(B) the geographic area to be served by the project;

(C) the percentage of low-income individuals (as described in subsection (b)) and individuals receiving assistance under a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.] in the area to be served by the project; and

(D) unemployment rates in the geographic areas to be served and (to the extent practicable) the jobs available and skills necessary to fill those vacancies in such areas.


(2) In approving applications under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to applications proposing to serve those areas containing the highest percentage of individuals receiving assistance under a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.].


(d) Administration

Each nonprofit organization participating in a project conducted under this section shall provide assurances in its agreement with the Secretary that it has or will have a cooperative relationship with the agency responsible for administering the the 2

2 So in original.

 State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.] in the area served by the project.


(e) Authorization of appropriations

For the purpose of conducting projects under this section, there is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $25,000,000 for any fiscal year.

<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c01b002-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901"><ns0:num value="9901">§ 9901.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Purposes and goals</ns0:heading>
<ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The purposes of this chapter are—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c01b003-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to provide assistance to States and local communities, working through a network of community action agencies and other neighborhood-based organizations, for the reduction of poverty, the revitalization of low-income communities, and the empowerment of low-income families and individuals in rural and urban areas to become fully self-sufficient (particularly families who are attempting to transition off a State program carried out under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act (<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s601">42 U.S.C. 601</ns0:ref> et seq.)); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c01b004-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> to accomplish the goals described in paragraph (1) through—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c01b005-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the strengthening of community capabilities for planning and coordinating the use of a broad range of Federal, State, local, and other assistance (including private resources) related to the elimination of poverty, so that this assistance can be used in a manner responsive to local needs and conditions;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c01b006-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the organization of a range of services related to the needs of low-income families and individuals, so that these services may have a measurable and potentially major impact on the causes of poverty in the community and may help the families and individuals to achieve self-sufficiency;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c01b007-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/C"><ns0:num value="C">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the greater use of innovative and effective community-based approaches to attacking the causes and effects of poverty and of community breakdown;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c01b008-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/D"><ns0:num value="D">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the maximum participation of residents of the low-income communities and members of the groups served by programs assisted through the block grants made under this chapter to empower such residents and members to respond to the unique problems and needs within their communities; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c01b009-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/E"><ns0:num value="E">(E)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> the broadening of the resource base of programs directed to the elimination of poverty so as to secure a more active role in the provision of services for—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c01b00a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/E/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> private, religious, charitable, and neighborhood-based organizations; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c01b00b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9901/2/E/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> individual citizens, and business, labor, and professional groups, who are able to influence the quantity and quality of opportunities and services for the poor.</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>

<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I86" topic="executiveOrder" id="id9c042015-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">Ex. Ord. No. 13969. Expanding Educational Opportunity Through School Choice</ns0:heading>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Ex. Ord. No. 13969, <ns0:date date="2020-12-28">Dec. 28, 2020</ns0:date>, 86 F.R. 219, provided:</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, and in order to ensure the education, health, safety, and well-being of America’s children, our most essential resource upon which the future of our great Nation depends, it is hereby ordered as follows:</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0"><ns0:inline class="small-caps">Section</ns0:inline> 1. <ns0:i>Purpose</ns0:i>. As part of their efforts to address the public health challenges and uncertainties posed by the COVID–19 pandemic, State and local officials shut down in-person learning for the vast majority of our more than 56 million elementary and secondary school students beginning in late February and early March of this year. Since then, however, our Nation has identified effective measures to facilitate the safe resumption of in-person learning, and the Federal Government has provided more than $13 billion to States and school districts to implement those measures.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">The prolonged deprivation of in-person learning opportunities has produced undeniably dire consequences for the children of this country. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has stated that school attendance is negatively correlated with a child’s risk of depression and various types of abuse. States have seen substantial declines in reports of child maltreatment while school buildings have been closed, indicating that allegations are going unreported. These reductions are driven in part by social isolation from the schoolteachers and support staff with whom students typically interact and who have an obligation to report suspected child maltreatment. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) has also found that school closures have a “substantial impact on food security and physical activity for children and families.” Additionally, a recent survey of educators found student absences from school, including virtual learning, have nearly doubled during the pandemic, and as AAP has noted, chronic absenteeism is associated with alcohol and drug use, teenage pregnancy, juvenile delinquency, and suicide attempts.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">School closures are especially difficult for families with children with special needs. Schools provide not only academic supports for students with special needs, but they also provide much-needed in-person therapies and services, including physical and occupational therapies. A recent survey found that 80 percent of children with special needs are not receiving the services and supports to which they are entitled and that approximately 40 percent of children with special needs are receiving no services or supports. Moreover, the survey found that virtual learning may not be fully accessible to these students, as children with special needs are twice as likely to receive little or no remote learning and to be dissatisfied with the remote learning received.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Low-income and minority children are also disproportionately affected by school closures. In low-income zip codes, students’ math progress decreased by nearly 50 percent while school buildings were closed in the spring, and the math progress of students in middle-income zip codes fell by almost a third during the same period. A recent analysis projected that, if in-person classes do not fully resume until January 2021, Hispanic, Black, and low-income students will lose 9.2, 10.3, and 12.4 months of learning, respectively.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">A failure to quickly resume in-person learning options is likely to have long-term economic effects on children and their families. According to a recent study, if in-person classes do not fully resume until January 2021, the average student could lose $61,000 to $82,000 in lifetime earnings, or the equivalent of a year of full-time work. Additionally, in 2019, more than 90 percent of children under the age of 18 had at least one employed parent. Many employed parents do not have the option of engaging in remote work that allows them the flexibility to supervise their children during the day when in-person learning options are not available. Without the resumption of in-person learning opportunities, the economic and social harms resulting from such lost employment opportunities will continue to compound.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">To help mitigate these harms, the Department of Health and Human Services recently announced additional relief for low-income parents by allowing States to use funds available through the Child Care and Development Fund to subsidize child care services and services that supplement academic instruction for children under the age of 13 who are participating in virtual instruction. Nevertheless, virtual instruction is an inadequate substitute for in-person learning opportunities and this aid is insufficient to meet current needs.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">While some families, especially those with financial means, have been able to mitigate school disruptions through in-person options such as homeschooling, private schools, charter schools, and innovative models like microschools and “learning pods,” for many families, their children’s residentially assigned public school remains their only financially available option. Unfortunately, more than 50 percent of all public-school students in the United States began school remotely this fall. These children, including those with special needs, are being underserved due to the public education system’s failure to provide in-person learning options.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Students whose families pay tuition for their education are also facing significant hardships due to the economic disruptions caused by the pandemic. Scores of private schools, including approximately 100 Catholic schools, have permanently closed since the onset of COVID–19, and more than half of our Nation’s private schools are believed to have lost enrollment due to the pandemic. These closures and declining enrollments are harmful to students, bad for communities, and likely to impose increased strain on public school systems.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">I am committed to ensuring that all children of our great Nation have access to the educational resources they need to obtain a high-quality education and to improving students’ safety and well-being, including by empowering families with emergency learning scholarships.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0"><ns0:inline class="small-caps">Sec.</ns0:inline> 2. <ns0:i>Providing Emergency Learning Scholarships for Students</ns0:i>. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall take steps, consistent with law, to allow funds available through the Community Services Block Grant program to be used by grantees and eligible entities to provide emergency learning scholarships to disadvantaged families for use by any child without access to in-person learning. These scholarships may be used for:</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(i) tuition and fees for a private or parochial school;</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(ii) homeschool, microschool, or learning-pod costs;</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(iii) special education and related services, including therapies; or</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(iv) tutoring or remedial education.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0"><ns0:inline class="small-caps">Sec.</ns0:inline> 3. <ns0:i>General Provisions</ns0:i>. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.</ns0:p>
<ns0:signature>
<ns0:name>Donald J. Trump.</ns0:name>
</ns0:signature>
</ns0:note>
</ns0:notes>
</ns0:section>
<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c042016-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902"><ns0:num value="9902">§ 9902.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Definitions</ns0:heading>
<ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">In this chapter:</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042017-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Eligible entity; family literacy services</ns0:heading><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042018-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/1/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Eligible entity</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The term “eligible entity” means an entity—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c042019-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/1/A/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that is an eligible entity described in paragraph (1) (as in effect on the day before <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">October 27, 1998</ns0:date>) as of the day before <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">October 27, 1998</ns0:date>, or is designated by the process described in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9909">section 9909 of this title</ns0:ref> (including an organization serving migrant or seasonal farmworkers that is so described or designated); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c04201a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/1/A/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that has a tripartite board or other mechanism described in subsection (a) or (b), as appropriate, of <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9910">section 9910 of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04201b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/1/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Family literacy services</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The term “family literacy services” has the meaning given the term in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9832">section 9832 of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04201c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Poverty line</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">The term “poverty line” means the official poverty line defined by the Office of Management and Budget based on the most recent data available from the Bureau of the Census. The Secretary shall revise annually (or at any shorter interval the Secretary determines to be feasible and desirable) the poverty line, which shall be used as a criterion of eligibility in the community services block grant program established under this chapter. The required revision shall be accomplished by multiplying the official poverty line by the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the annual or other interval immediately preceding the time at which the revision is made. Whenever a State determines that it serves the objectives of the block grant program established under this chapter, the State may revise the poverty line to not to exceed 125 percent of the official poverty line otherwise applicable under this paragraph.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04201d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/3"><ns0:num value="3" class="bold">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Private, nonprofit organization</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">The term “private, nonprofit organization” includes a religious organization, to which the provisions of <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9920">section 9920 of this title</ns0:ref> shall apply.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04201e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/4"><ns0:num value="4" class="bold">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Secretary</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04201f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9902/5"><ns0:num value="5" class="bold">(5)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> State</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">The term “State” means each of the several States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, the United States Virgin Islands, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>

</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042026-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Reservations</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">Of the amounts appropriated under subsection (a) for each fiscal year, the Secretary shall reserve—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c042027-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> ½ of 1 percent for carrying out <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9905">section 9905 of this title</ns0:ref> (relating to payments for territories);</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c042028-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> 1½ percent for activities authorized in sections 9913 through 9918 of this title, of which—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042029-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b/2/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> not less than ½ of the amount reserved by the Secretary under this paragraph shall be distributed directly to eligible entities, organizations, or associations described in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9913/c/2">section 9913(c)(2) of this title</ns0:ref> for the purpose of carrying out activities described in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9913/c">section 9913(c) of this title</ns0:ref>; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c04202a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b/2/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> ½ of the remainder of the amount reserved by the Secretary under this paragraph shall be used by the Secretary to carry out evaluation and to assist States in carrying out corrective action activities and monitoring (to correct programmatic deficiencies of eligible entities), as described in sections 9914(c) and 9913 of this title; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c04202b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> 9 percent for carrying out <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9921">section 9921 of this title</ns0:ref> (relating to discretionary activities) and <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9917/b/2">section 9917(b)(2) of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:content>

<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c042030-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9904"><ns0:num value="9904">§ 9904.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Establishment of block grant program</ns0:heading><ns0:content>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary is authorized to establish a community services block grant program and make grants through the program to States to ameliorate the causes of poverty in communities within the States.</ns0:p>

L. 105–285</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
</ns0:notes>
</ns0:section>
<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c042035-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9905"><ns0:num value="9905">§ 9905.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Distribution to territories</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042036-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9905/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Apportionment</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary shall apportion the amount reserved under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b/1">section 9903(b)(1) of this title</ns0:ref> for each fiscal year on the basis of need among Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042037-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9905/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Application</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">Each jurisdiction to which subsection (a) applies may receive a grant under this section for the amount apportioned under subsection (a) on submitting to the Secretary, and obtaining approval of, an application, containing provisions that describe the programs for which assistance is sought under this section, that is prepared in accordance with, and contains the information described in, <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9908">section 9908 of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:sourceCredit id="id9c042038-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">(<ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s675A">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 675A</ns0:ref>, as added <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285/tII/s201">Pub. L. 105–285, title II, § 201</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">Oct. 27, 1998</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/112/2730">112 Stat. 2730</ns0:ref>.)</ns0:sourceCredit>
<ns0:notes type="uscNote" id="id9c042039-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" role="crossHeading" topic="editorialNotes" id="id9c04203a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered"><ns0:b>Editorial Notes</ns0:b></ns0:heading></ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" topic="priorProvisions" id="id9c04203b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">Prior Provisions</ns0:heading><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Prior sections 9905 and 9905a were omitted in the general amendment of this chapter by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285">Pub. L. 105–285</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Section 9905, <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s676">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 676</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1981-08-13">Aug. 13, 1981</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/95/516">95 Stat. 516</ns0:ref>, related to establishment and functions of the Office of Community Services.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Section 9905a, <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s676A">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 676A</ns0:ref>, as added <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/98/558/tII/s203/d">Pub. L. 98–558, title II, § 203(d)</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1984-10-30">Oct. 30, 1984</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/98/2885">98 Stat. 2885</ns0:ref>; amended <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/99/425/tIV/s403/a/2">Pub. L. 99–425, title IV, § 403(a)(2)</ns0:ref>–(4), <ns0:date date="1986-09-30">Sept. 30, 1986</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/100/968">100 Stat. 968</ns0:ref>, 969; <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/101/501/tIV/s404/c">Pub. L. 101–501, title IV, § 404(c)</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1990-11-03">Nov. 3, 1990</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/104/1252">104 Stat. 1252</ns0:ref>, related to procedures for review of termination or reduction of funding.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
</ns0:notes>
</ns0:section>
<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c04203c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906"><ns0:num value="9906">§ 9906.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Allotments and payments to States</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04203d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Allotments in general</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary shall, from the amount appropriated under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/a">section 9903(a) of this title</ns0:ref> for each fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b">section 9903(b) of this title</ns0:ref>, allot to each State (subject to <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9911">section 9911 of this title</ns0:ref>) an amount that bears the same ratio to such remaining amount as the amount received by the State for fiscal year 1981 under section 2808 <ns0:ref class="footnoteRef" idref="fn003923">1</ns0:ref><ns0:note type="footnote" id="fn003923"><ns0:num>1</ns0:num> See References in Text note below.</ns0:note> of this title bore to the total amount received by all States for fiscal year 1981 under such section, except—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c04203e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/a/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that no State shall receive less than ¼ of 1 percent of the amount appropriated under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/a">section 9903(a) of this title</ns0:ref> for such fiscal year; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c04203f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/a/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> as provided in subsection (b).</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042040-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Allotments in years with greater available funds</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042041-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/b/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Minimum allotments</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), if the amount appropriated under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/a">section 9903(a) of this title</ns0:ref> for a fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/b">section 9903(b) of this title</ns0:ref> exceeds $345,000,000, the Secretary shall allot to each State not less than ½ of 1 percent of the amount appropriated under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/a">section 9903(a) of this title</ns0:ref> for such fiscal year.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042042-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/b/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Maintenance of fiscal year 1990 levels</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Paragraph (1) shall not apply with respect to a fiscal year if the amount allotted under subsection (a) to any State for that year is less than the amount allotted under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9903/a/1">section 9903(a)(1) of this title</ns0:ref> (as in effect on <ns0:date date="1989-09-30">September 30, 1989</ns0:date>) to such State for fiscal year 1990.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042043-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/b/3"><ns0:num value="3" class="bold">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Maximum allotments</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">The amount allotted under paragraph (1) to a State for a fiscal year shall be reduced, if necessary, so that the aggregate amount allotted to such State under such paragraph and subsection (a) does not exceed 140 percent of the aggregate amount allotted to such State under the corresponding provisions of this chapter for the preceding fiscal year.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042044-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/c"><ns0:num value="c" class="bold">(c)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Payments</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary shall make grants to eligible States for the allotments described in subsections (a) and (b). The Secretary shall make payments for the grants in accordance with <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t31/s6503/a">section 6503(a) of title 31</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042045-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9906/d"><ns0:num value="d" class="bold">(d)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definition</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">In this section, the term “State” does not include Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:sourceCredit id="id9c042046-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">(<ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s675B">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 675B</ns0:ref>, as added <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285/tII/s201">Pub. L. 105–285, title II, § 201</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">Oct. 27, 1998</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/112/2730">112 Stat. 2730</ns0:ref>.)</ns0:sourceCredit>
<ns0:notes type="uscNote" id="id9c042047-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" role="crossHeading" topic="editorialNotes" id="id9c042048-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered"><ns0:b>Editorial Notes</ns0:b></ns0:heading></ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I75" topic="referencesInText" id="id9c042049-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">References in Text</ns0:heading><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0"><ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s2808">Section 2808 of this title</ns0:ref>, referred to in subsec. (a), was repealed by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s683/a">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 683(a)</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1981-08-13">Aug. 13, 1981</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/95/519">95 Stat. 519</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" topic="priorProvisions" id="id9c04204a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">Prior Provisions</ns0:heading><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">A prior section 9906, <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s677">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 677</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1981-08-13">Aug. 13, 1981</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/95/516">95 Stat. 516</ns0:ref>, contained nondiscrimination provisions, prior to the general amendment of this chapter by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285">Pub. L. 105–285</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
</ns0:notes>
</ns0:section>
<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c04204b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907"><ns0:num value="9907">§ 9907.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Uses of funds</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04204c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Grants to eligible entities and other organizations</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04204d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/a/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Not less than 90 percent of the funds made available to a State under section 9905 or 9906 of this title shall be used by the State to make grants for the purposes described in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9901">section 9901 of this title</ns0:ref> to eligible entities.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04204e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/a/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Obligational authority</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Funds distributed to eligible entities through grants made in accordance with paragraph (1) for a fiscal year shall be available for obligation during that fiscal year and the succeeding fiscal year, subject to paragraph (3).</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04204f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/a/3"><ns0:num value="3" class="bold">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Recapture and redistribution of unobligated funds</ns0:heading><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042050-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/a/3/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Amount</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">Beginning on <ns0:date date="2000-10-01">October 1, 2000</ns0:date>, a State may recapture and redistribute funds distributed to an eligible entity through a grant made under paragraph (1) that are unobligated at the end of a fiscal year if such unobligated funds exceed 20 percent of the amount so distributed to such eligible entity for such fiscal year.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042051-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/a/3/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Redistribution</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">In redistributing funds recaptured in accordance with this paragraph, States shall redistribute such funds to an eligible entity, or require the original recipient of the funds to redistribute the funds to a private, nonprofit organization, located within the community served by the original recipient of the funds, for activities consistent with the purposes of this chapter.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042052-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Statewide activities</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042053-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Use of remainder</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">If a State uses less than 100 percent of the grant or allotment received under section 9905 or 9906 of this title to make grants under subsection (a), the State shall use the remainder of the grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title (subject to paragraph (2)) for activities that may include—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042054-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> providing training and technical assistance to those entities in need of such training and assistance;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042055-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> coordinating State-operated programs and services, and at the option of the State, locally-operated programs and services, targeted to low-income children and families with services provided by eligible entities and other organizations funded under this chapter, including detailing appropriate employees of State or local agencies to entities funded under this chapter, to ensure increased access to services provided by such State or local agencies;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042056-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/C"><ns0:num value="C">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:content> supporting statewide coordination and communication among eligible entities;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042057-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/D"><ns0:num value="D">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:content> analyzing the distribution of funds made available under this chapter within the State to determine if such funds have been targeted to the areas of greatest need;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042058-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/E"><ns0:num value="E">(E)</ns0:num><ns0:content> supporting asset-building programs for low-income individuals, such as programs supporting individual development accounts;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c042059-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/F"><ns0:num value="F">(F)</ns0:num><ns0:content> supporting innovative programs and activities conducted by community action agencies or other neighborhood-based organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and promote community revitalization;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c04205a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/G"><ns0:num value="G">(G)</ns0:num><ns0:content> supporting State charity tax credits as described in subsection (c); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c04205b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/1/H"><ns0:num value="H">(H)</ns0:num><ns0:content> supporting other activities, consistent with the purposes of this chapter.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04205c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/b/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Administrative cap</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">No State may spend more than the greater of $55,000, or 5 percent, of the grant received under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9905">section 9905 of this title</ns0:ref> or State allotment received under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9906">section 9906 of this title</ns0:ref> for administrative expenses, including monitoring activities. Funds to be spent for such expenses shall be taken from the portion of the grant under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9905">section 9905 of this title</ns0:ref> or State allotment that remains after the State makes grants to eligible entities under subsection (a). The cost of activities conducted under paragraph (1)(A) shall not be considered to be administrative expenses. The startup cost and cost of administrative activities conducted under subsection (c) shall be considered to be administrative expenses.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04205d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c"><ns0:num value="c" class="bold">(c)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Charity tax credit</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04205e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Subject to paragraph (2), if there is in effect under State law a charity tax credit, the State may use for any purpose the amount of the allotment that is available for expenditure under subsection (b).</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04205f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Limit</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">The aggregate amount a State may use under paragraph (1) during a fiscal year shall not exceed 100 percent of the revenue loss of the State during the fiscal year that is attributable to the charity tax credit, as determined by the Secretary of the Treasury without regard to any such revenue loss occurring before <ns0:date date="1999-01-01">January 1, 1999</ns0:date>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042060-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3"><ns0:num value="3" class="bold">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definitions and rules</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">In this subsection:</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042061-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Charity tax credit</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The term “charity tax credit” means a nonrefundable credit against State income tax (or, in the case of a State that does not impose an income tax, a comparable benefit) that is allowable for contributions, in cash or in kind, to qualified charities.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042062-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Qualified charity</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042063-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">The term “qualified charity” means any organization—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c042064-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> that is—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042065-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i/I/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> described in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t26/s501/c/3">section 501(c)(3) of title 26</ns0:ref> and exempt from tax under section 501(a) of such title;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042066-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i/I/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an eligible entity; or</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042067-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i/I/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a public housing agency as defined in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s1437a/b/6">section 1437a(b)(6) of this title</ns0:ref>;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c042068-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that is certified by the appropriate State authority as meeting the requirements of clauses (iii) and (iv); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c042069-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/i/III"><ns0:num value="III">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:content> if such organization is otherwise required to file a return under section 6033 of such title, that elects to treat the information required to be furnished by clause (v) as being specified in section 6033(b) of such title.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04206a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Certain contributions to collection organizations treated as contributions to qualified charity</ns0:heading><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04206b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/ii/I"><ns0:num value="I" class="bold">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">A contribution to a collection organization shall be treated as a contribution to a qualified charity if the donor designates in writing that the contribution is for the qualified charity.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04206c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/ii/II"><ns0:num value="II" class="bold">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Collection organization</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">The term “collection organization” means an organization described in section 501(c)(3) of such title and exempt from tax under section 501(a) of such title—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c04206d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/ii/II/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that solicits and collects gifts and grants that, by agreement, are distributed to qualified charities;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c04206e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/ii/II/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that distributes to qualified charities at least 90 percent of the gifts and grants the organization receives that are designated for such qualified charities; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c04206f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/ii/II/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that meets the requirements of clause (vi).</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042070-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iii"><ns0:num value="iii" class="bold">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Charity must primarily assist poor individuals</ns0:heading><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042071-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iii/I"><ns0:num value="I" class="bold">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">An organization meets the requirements of this clause only if the appropriate State authority reasonably expects that the predominant activity of such organization will be the provision of direct services within the United States to individuals and families whose annual incomes generally do not exceed 185 percent of the poverty line in order to prevent or alleviate poverty among such individuals and families.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042072-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iii/II"><ns0:num value="II" class="bold">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> No recordkeeping in certain cases</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">An organization shall not be required to establish or maintain records with respect to the incomes of individuals and families for purposes of subclause (I) if such individuals or families are members of groups that are generally recognized as including substantially only individuals and families described in subclause (I).</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042073-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iii/III"><ns0:num value="III" class="bold">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Food aid and homeless shelters</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">Except as otherwise provided by the appropriate State authority, for purposes of subclause (I), services to individuals in the form of—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042074-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iii/III/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> donations of food or meals; or</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042075-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iii/III/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> temporary shelter to homeless individuals;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>

<ns0:continuation style="-uslm-lc:I56" class="indent4 firstIndent-2">  shall be treated as provided to individuals described in subclause (I) if the location and provision of such services are such that the service provider may reasonably conclude that the beneficiaries of such services are predominantly individuals described in subclause (I).</ns0:continuation>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042076-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iv"><ns0:num value="iv" class="bold">(iv)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Minimum expense requirement</ns0:heading><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042077-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iv/I"><ns0:num value="I" class="bold">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">An organization meets the requirements of this clause only if the appropriate State authority reasonably expects that the annual poverty program expenses of such organization will not be less than 75 percent of the annual aggregate expenses of such organization.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I72" class="indent6 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042078-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iv/II"><ns0:num value="II" class="bold">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Poverty program expense</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4">For purposes of subclause (I)—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580469" class="indent7 firstIndent-2 bold" id="id9c042079-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iv/II/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:heading> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5">The term “poverty program expense” means any expense in providing direct services referred to in clause (iii).</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580469" class="indent7 firstIndent-2 bold" id="id9c04207a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/iv/II/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Exceptions</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5">Such term shall not include any management or general expense, any expense for the purpose of influencing legislation (as defined in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t26/s4911/d">section 4911(d) of title 26</ns0:ref>), any expense for the purpose of fundraising, any expense for a legal service provided on behalf of any individual referred to in clause (iii), any expense for providing tuition assistance relating to compulsory school attendance, and any expense that consists of a payment to an affiliate of the organization.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04207b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/v"><ns0:num value="v" class="bold">(v)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Reporting requirement</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">The information required to be furnished under this clause about an organization is—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c04207c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/v/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the percentages determined by dividing the following categories of the organization’s expenses for the year by the total expenses of the organization for the year: expenses for direct services, management expenses, general expenses, fundraising expenses, and payments to affiliates; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c04207d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/v/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the category or categories (including food, shelter, education, substance abuse prevention or treatment, job training, or other) of services that constitute predominant activities of the organization.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c04207e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vi"><ns0:num value="vi" class="bold">(vi)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Additional requirements for collection organizations</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">The requirements of this clause are met if the organization—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c04207f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vi/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> maintains separate accounting for revenues and expenses; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c042080-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vi/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> makes available to the public information on the administrative and fundraising costs of the organization, and information as to the organizations receiving funds from the organization and the amount of such funds.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042081-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vii"><ns0:num value="vii" class="bold">(vii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Special rule for States requiring tax uniformity</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">In the case of a State—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c042082-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vii/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that has a constitutional requirement of tax uniformity; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id9c042083-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vii/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> that, as of <ns0:date date="1997-12-31">December 31, 1997</ns0:date>, imposed a tax on personal income with—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042084-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vii/II/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a single flat rate applicable to all earned and unearned income (except insofar as any amount is not taxed pursuant to tax forgiveness provisions); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id9c042085-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/3/B/vii/II/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> no generally available exemptions or deductions to individuals;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>

<ns0:continuation style="-uslm-lc:I66" class="indent3 firstIndent-1"> the requirement of paragraph (2) shall be treated as met if the amount of the credit described in paragraph (2) is limited to a uniform percentage (but not greater than 25 percent) of State personal income tax liability (determined without regard to credits).</ns0:continuation>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042086-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/4"><ns0:num value="4" class="bold">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Limitation on use of funds for startup and administrative activities</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Except to the extent provided in subsection (b)(2), no part of the aggregate amount a State uses under paragraph (1) may be used to pay for the cost of the startup and administrative activities conducted under this subsection.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042087-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/5"><ns0:num value="5" class="bold">(5)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Prohibition on use of funds for legal services or tuition assistance</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">No part of the aggregate amount a State uses under paragraph (1) may be used to provide legal services or to provide tuition assistance related to compulsory education requirements (not including tuition assistance for tutoring, camps, skills development, or other supplemental services or training).</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c042088-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9907/c/6"><ns0:num value="6" class="bold">(6)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Prohibition on supplanting funds</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">No part of the aggregate amount a State uses under paragraph (1) may be used to supplant non-Federal funds that would be available, in the absence of Federal funds, to offset a revenue loss of the State attributable to a charity tax credit.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>

L. 105–285, title II, § 201</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">Oct. 27, 1998</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/112/2731">112 Stat. 2731</ns0:ref>.)</ns0:sourceCredit>
