<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c069193-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922"><ns0:num value="9922">§ 9922.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Community food and nutrition programs</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c069194-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Grants</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary may, through grants to public and private, nonprofit agencies, provide for community-based, local, statewide, and national programs—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c069195-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/a/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to coordinate private and public food assistance resources, wherever the grant recipient involved determines such coordination to be inadequate, to better serve low-income populations;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c069196-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/a/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to assist low-income communities to identify potential sponsors of child nutrition programs and to initiate such programs in underserved or unserved areas; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c069197-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/a/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to develop innovative approaches at the State and local level to meet the nutrition needs of low-income individuals.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c069198-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Allotments and distribution of funds</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c069199-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Not to exceed $6,000,000 in appropriations</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Of the amount appropriated for a fiscal year to carry out this section (but not to exceed $6,000,000), the Secretary shall distribute funds for grants under subsection (a) as follows:</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c06919a-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/1/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Allotments</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">From a portion equal to 60 percent of such amount (but not to exceed $3,600,000), the Secretary shall allot for grants to eligible agencies for statewide programs in each State the amount that bears the same ratio to such portion as the low-income and unemployed population of such State bears to the low-income and unemployed population of all the States.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c06919b-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/1/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Competitive grants</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">From a portion equal to 40 percent of such amount (but not to exceed $2,400,000), the Secretary shall make grants on a competitive basis to eligible agencies for local and statewide programs.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c06919c-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Greater available appropriations</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">Any amounts appropriated for a fiscal year to carry out this section in excess of $6,000,000 shall be allotted as follows:</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c06919d-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/2/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Allotments</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The Secretary shall use 40 percent of such excess to allot for grants under subsection (a) to eligible agencies for statewide programs in each State an amount that bears the same ratio to 40 percent of such excess as the low-income and unemployed population of such State bears to the low-income and unemployed population of all the States.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c06919e-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/2/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Competitive grants for local and statewide programs</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The Secretary shall use 40 percent of such excess to make grants under subsection (a) on a competitive basis to eligible agencies for local and statewide programs.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c06919f-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/2/C"><ns0:num value="C" class="bold">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Competitive grants for nationwide programs</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The Secretary shall use the remaining 20 percent of such excess to make grants under subsection (a) on a competitive basis to eligible agencies for nationwide programs, including programs benefiting Indians, as defined in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9911">section 9911 of this title</ns0:ref>, and migrant or seasonal farmworkers.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691a0-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/3"><ns0:num value="3" class="bold">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Eligibility for allotments for statewide programs</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">To be eligible to receive an allotment under paragraph (1)(A) or (2)(A), an eligible agency shall demonstrate that the proposed program is statewide in scope and represents a comprehensive and coordinated effort to alleviate hunger within the State.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691a1-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/4"><ns0:num value="4" class="bold">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Minimum allotments for statewide programs</ns0:heading><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691a2-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/4/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">From the amounts allotted under paragraphs (1)(A) and (2)(A), the minimum total allotment for each State for each fiscal year shall be—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c0691a3-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/4/A/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> $15,000 if the total amount appropriated to carry out this section is not less than $7,000,000 but less than $10,000,000;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c0691a4-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/4/A/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> $20,000 if the total amount appropriated to carry out this section is not less than $10,000,000 but less than $15,000,000; or</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id9c0691a5-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/4/A/iii"><ns0:num value="iii">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> $30,000 if the total amount appropriated to carry out this section is not less than $15,000,000.</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691a6-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/4/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definition</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">In this paragraph, the term “State” does not include Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691a7-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/b/5"><ns0:num value="5" class="bold">(5)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Maximum grants</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">From funds made available under paragraphs (1)(B) and (2)(B) for any fiscal year, the Secretary may not make grants under subsection (a) to an eligible agency in an aggregate amount exceeding $50,000. From funds made available under paragraph (2)(C) for any fiscal year, the Secretary may not make grants under subsection (a) to an eligible agency in an aggregate amount exceeding $300,000.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691a8-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/c"><ns0:num value="c" class="bold">(c)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Report</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">For each fiscal year, the Secretary shall prepare and submit, to the Committee on Education and the Workforce of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Labor and Human Resources of the Senate, a report concerning the grants made under this section. Such report shall include—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691a9-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/c/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a list of grant recipients;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691aa-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/c/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> information on the amount of funding awarded to each grant recipient; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691ab-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/c/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a summary of the activities performed by the grant recipients with funding awarded under this section and a description of the manner in which such activities meet the objectives described in subsection (a).</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691ac-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9922/d"><ns0:num value="d" class="bold">(d)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Authorization of appropriations</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section such sums as may be necessary for each of fiscal years 1999 through 2003.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>

L. 105–285, title II, § 201</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">Oct. 27, 1998</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/112/2752">112 Stat. 2752</ns0:ref>.)</ns0:sourceCredit>
<ns0:notes type="uscNote" id="id9c0691ae-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" role="crossHeading" topic="editorialNotes" id="id9c0691af-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered"><ns0:b>Editorial Notes</ns0:b></ns0:heading></ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" topic="priorProvisions" id="id9c0691b0-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">Prior Provisions</ns0:heading><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">A prior <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/s681">section 681 of Pub. L. 97–35</ns0:ref> was classified to <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9910">section 9910 of this title</ns0:ref>, prior to the general amendment of this chapter by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285">Pub. L. 105–285</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" role="crossHeading" topic="statutoryNotes" id="id9c0691b1-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered"><ns0:b>Statutory Notes and Related Subsidiaries</ns0:b></ns0:heading></ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I78" topic="changeOfName" id="id9c0691b2-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">Change of Name</ns0:heading>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Committee on Labor and Human Resources of Senate changed to Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of Senate by Senate Resolution No. 20, One Hundred Sixth Congress, <ns0:date date="1999-01-19">Jan. 19, 1999</ns0:date>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
</ns0:notes>
</ns0:section>
<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c0691b3-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923"><ns0:num value="9923">§ 9923.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> National or regional programs designed to provide instructional activities for low-income youth</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691b4-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> General authority</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary is authorized to make a grant to an eligible service provider to administer national or regional programs to provide instructional activities for low-income youth. In making such a grant, the Secretary shall give priority to eligible service providers that have a demonstrated ability to operate such a program.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691b5-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Program requirements</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">Any instructional activity carried out by an eligible service provider receiving a grant under this section shall be carried out on the campus of an institution of higher education (as defined in section 1141(a) <ns0:ref class="footnoteRef" idref="fn003924">1</ns0:ref><ns0:note type="footnote" id="fn003924"><ns0:num>1</ns0:num> See References in Text note below.</ns0:note> of title 20) and shall include—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691b6-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/b/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> access to the facilities and resources of such an institution;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691b7-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/b/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an initial medical examination and follow-up referral or treatment, without charge, for youth during their participation in such activity;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691b8-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/b/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> at least one nutritious meal daily, without charge, for participating youth during each day of participation;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691b9-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/b/4"><ns0:num value="4">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:content> high quality instruction in a variety of sports (that shall include swimming and that may include dance and any other high quality recreational activity) provided by coaches and teachers from institutions of higher education and from elementary and secondary schools (as defined in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t20/s7801">section 7801 of title 20</ns0:ref>); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691ba-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/b/5"><ns0:num value="5">(5)</ns0:num><ns0:content> enrichment instruction and information on matters relating to the well-being of youth, to include educational opportunities and information on study practices, education for the prevention of drug and alcohol abuse, and information on health and nutrition, career opportunities, and family and job responsibilities.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691bb-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/c"><ns0:num value="c" class="bold">(c)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Advisory committee; partnerships</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The eligible service provider shall, in each community in which a program is funded under this section—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691bc-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/c/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> ensure that—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c0691bd-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/c/1/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a community-based advisory committee is established, with representatives from local youth, family, and social service organizations, schools, entities providing park and recreation services, and other community-based organizations serving high-risk youth; or</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id9c0691be-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/c/1/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an existing community-based advisory board, commission, or committee with similar membership is utilized to serve as the committee described in subparagraph (A); and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691bf-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/c/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> enter into formal partnerships with youth-serving organizations or other appropriate social service entities in order to link program participants with year-round services in their home communities that support and continue the objectives of this chapter.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691c0-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/d"><ns0:num value="d" class="bold">(d)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Eligible providers</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">A service provider that is a national private, nonprofit organization, a coalition of such organizations, or a private, nonprofit organization applying jointly with a business concern shall be eligible to apply for a grant under this section if—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691c1-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/d/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the applicant has demonstrated experience in operating a program providing instruction to low-income youth;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691c2-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/d/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the applicant agrees to contribute an amount (in cash or in kind, fairly evaluated) of not less than 25 percent of the amount requested, for the program funded through the grant;</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691c3-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/d/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the applicant agrees to use no funds from a grant authorized under this section for administrative expenses; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c0691c4-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/d/4"><ns0:num value="4">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the applicant agrees to comply with the regulations or program guidelines promulgated by the Secretary for use of funds made available through the grant.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691c5-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/e"><ns0:num value="e" class="bold">(e)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Application process</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">To be eligible to receive a grant under this section, a service provider shall submit to the Secretary, for approval, an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691c6-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/f"><ns0:num value="f" class="bold">(f)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Promulgation of regulations or program guidelines</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary shall promulgate regulations or program guidelines to ensure funds made available through a grant made under this section are used in accordance with the objectives of this chapter.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c0691c7-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9923/g"><ns0:num value="g" class="bold">(g)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Authorization of appropriations</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">There are authorized to be appropriated $15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 1999 through 2003 for grants to carry out this section.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>

<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c08dbc1-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9924"><ns0:num value="9924">§ 9924.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> References</ns0:heading><ns0:content>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">Any reference in any provision of law to the poverty line set forth in section 624 or 625 of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 shall be construed to be a reference to the poverty line defined in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9902">section 9902 of this title</ns0:ref>. Except as otherwise provided, any reference in any provision of law to any community action agency designated under title II of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 shall be construed to be a reference to an entity eligible to receive funds under the community services block grant program.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content><ns0:sourceCredit id="id9c08dbc2-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">(<ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s683">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 683</ns0:ref>, as added <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285/tII/s201">Pub. L. 105–285, title II, § 201</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1998-10-27">Oct. 27, 1998</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/112/2755">112 Stat. 2755</ns0:ref>.)</ns0:sourceCredit>
<ns0:notes type="uscNote" id="id9c08dbc3-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" role="crossHeading" topic="editorialNotes" id="id9c08dbc4-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered"><ns0:b>Editorial Notes</ns0:b></ns0:heading></ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I75" topic="referencesInText" id="id9c08dbc5-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc">
<ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">References in Text</ns0:heading><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">The Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, referred to in text, is <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/88/452">Pub. L. 88–452</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1964-08-20">Aug. 20, 1964</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/78/508">78 Stat. 508</ns0:ref>. Title II of the Act was classified generally to subchapter II (§ 2781 et seq.) of chapter 34 of this title prior to repeal by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/tVI/s683/a">Pub. L. 97–35, title VI, § 683(a)</ns0:ref>, <ns0:date date="1981-08-13">Aug. 13, 1981</ns0:date>, <ns0:ref href="/us/stat/95/519">95 Stat. 519</ns0:ref>. Section 625 of the Act, which was subsequently renumbered section 624 of the Act and related to the poverty line, was classified to <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s2971d">section 2971d of this title</ns0:ref>, prior to repeal by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/s683/a">section 683(a) of Pub. L. 97–35</ns0:ref>. For complete classification of this Act to the Code, see Tables.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
<ns0:note style="-uslm-lc:I74" topic="priorProvisions" id="id9c08dbc6-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc"><ns0:heading class="centered smallCaps">Prior Provisions</ns0:heading><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">A prior <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/s683">section 683 of Pub. L. 97–35</ns0:ref> was classified to <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9911">section 9911 of this title</ns0:ref>, prior to the general amendment of this chapter by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285">Pub. L. 105–285</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Another prior <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/97/35/s683">section 683 of Pub. L. 97–35</ns0:ref> was renumbered section 684, and was classified to <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9912">section 9912 of this title</ns0:ref>, prior to the general amendment of this chapter by <ns0:ref href="/us/pl/105/285">Pub. L. 105–285</ns0:ref>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:note>
</ns0:notes>
</ns0:section>
<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c08dbc7-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925"><ns0:num value="9925">§ 9925.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Demonstration partnership agreements addressing needs of poor</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbc8-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> General authority</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbc9-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> In order to stimulate the development of new approaches to provide for greater self-sufficiency of the poor, to test and evaluate such new approaches, to disseminate project results and evaluation findings so that such approaches can be replicated, and to strengthen the integration, coordination, and redirection of activities to promote maximum self-sufficiency among the poor, the Secretary may make grants from funds appropriated under subsection (e) to eligible entities for the development and implementation of new and innovative approaches to deal with particularly critical needs or problems of the poor which are common to a number of communities. Grants may be made only with respect to applications which—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbca-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/1/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> involve activities which can be incorporated into or be closely coordinated with eligible entities’ ongoing programs;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbcb-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/1/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> involve significant new combinations of resources or new and innovative approaches involving partnership agreements;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbcc-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/1/C"><ns0:num value="C">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:content> are structured in a way that will, within the limits of the type of assistance or activities contemplated, most fully and effectively promote the purposes of the Community Services Block Grant Act [<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9901">42 U.S.C. 9901</ns0:ref> et seq.]; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbcd-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/1/D"><ns0:num value="D">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:content> contain an assurance that the applicant for such grants will obtain an independent, methodologically sound evaluation of the effectiveness of the activities carried out with such grant and will submit such evaluation to the Secretary.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbce-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> No grant may be made under this section unless an application is submitted to the Secretary at such time, in such manner, and containing or accompanied by such information, as the Secretary may require.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbcf-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/a/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Initial and subsequent grant awards may fully fund projects for periods of up to 3 years.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbd0-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Federal share; limitations</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbd1-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbd2-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/1/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Subject to subparagraph (B), grants awarded pursuant to this section shall be used for programs and shall not exceed 50 per centum of the cost of such programs.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbd3-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/1/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> After the first funding period for which an eligible entity receives a grant under this section to carry out a program, the amount of a subsequent grant made under this section to such entity to carry out such program may not exceed 80 percent of the amount of the grant previously received by such entity under this section to carry out such program.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbd4-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Non-Federal contributions may be in cash or in kind, fairly evaluated, including but not limited to plant, equipment, or services.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbd5-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Not more than one grant in each fiscal year may be made to any eligible entity, and no grant may exceed $350,000. Not more than 2 grants may be made under this section to an eligible entity to carry out a particular program.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbd6-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/4"><ns0:num value="4">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> No application may be approved for assistance under this section unless the Secretary is satisfied that—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbd7-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/4/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the activities to be carried out under the application will be in addition to, and not in substitution for, activities previously carried on without Federal assistance; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbd8-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/b/4/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> funds or other resources devoted to programs designed to meet the needs of the poor within the community, area, or State will not be diminished in order to provide the matching contributions required under this section.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbd9-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c"><ns0:num value="c" class="bold">(c)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Programs directed to special populations</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbda-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> In addition to the grant programs described in subsection (a), the Secretary may make grants to community action agencies for the purpose of enabling such agencies to demonstrate new approaches to dealing with the problems caused by entrenched, chronic unemployment and lack of economic opportunities for urban youth. Demonstrations shall include such activities as peer counseling, mentoring, development of job skills, assistance with social skills, community services, family literacy, parenting skills, opportunities for employment or entrepreneurship, and other services designed to assist such at-risk youth to continue their education, to secure meaningful employment, to perform community service, or to pursue other productive alternatives within the community.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbdb-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> Such grants may be made only with respect to applications that—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbdc-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/2/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> identify and describe the population to be served, the problems to be addressed, the overall approach and methods of outreach and recruitment to be used, and the services to be provided;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbdd-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/2/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> describe how the approach to be used differs from other approaches used for the population to be served by the project;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbde-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/2/C"><ns0:num value="C">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:content> describe the objectives of the project and contain a plan for measuring progress toward meeting those objectives; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbdf-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/2/D"><ns0:num value="D">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:content> contain assurances that the grantee will report on the progress and results of the demonstration at such times and in such manner as the Secretary shall require.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbe0-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Notwithstanding subsection (b), such grants shall not exceed 80 percent of the cost of such programs.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbe1-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/c/4"><ns0:num value="4">(4)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Such grants made under this subsection on a competitive basis shall be based on an annual competition determined by the Secretary. Grants made under this subsection shall not exceed $500,000.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbe2-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/d"><ns0:num value="d" class="bold">(d)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Dissemination of results</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">As soon as practicable, but not later than 180 days after the end of the fiscal year in which a recipient of a grant under this section completes the expenditure of such grant, the Secretary shall prepare and make available to each State and each eligible entity a description of the program carried out with such grant, any relevant information developed and results achieved, and a summary of the evaluation of such program received under subsection (a)(1)(D) so as to provide a model of innovative programs for other eligible entities.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbe3-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/e"><ns0:num value="e" class="bold">(e)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Replication of programs</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbe4-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/e/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> The Secretary shall annually identify programs that receive grants under this section that demonstrate a significant potential for dealing with particularly critical needs or problems of the poor that exist in a number of communities.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbe5-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/e/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Not less than 10 percent, and not more than 25 percent, of the funds appropriated for each fiscal year to carry out this section shall be available to make grants under this section to replicate in additional geographic areas programs identified under paragraph (1).</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbe6-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/f"><ns0:num value="f" class="bold">(f)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Omitted</ns0:heading><ns0:content />
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbe7-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/g"><ns0:num value="g" class="bold">(g)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definitions</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">As used in this section—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbe8-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/g/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the term “eligible entity” has the same meaning given such term by section 673(1) of the Community Services Block Grant Act (<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9902/1">42 U.S.C. 9902(1)</ns0:ref>), except that such term includes an organization that serves migrant and seasonal farm workers and that receives a grant under the Community Services Block Grant Act (<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9901">42 U.S.C. 9901</ns0:ref> et seq.) in the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year for which such organization requests a grant under this section; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dbe9-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/g/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbea-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/h"><ns0:num value="h" class="bold">(h)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Authorization of appropriations</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbeb-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/h/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> There are authorized to be appropriated $30,000,000 for fiscal year 1995, and such sums as may be necessary for fiscal years 1996, 1997, and 1998, to carry out this section.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbec-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/h/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Of the amounts appropriated for this section, not less than 30 percent and not more than 40 percent shall be used to carry out the programs authorized under subsection (c).</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbed-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9925/h/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> In addition to sums which are required to carry out the evaluation, reporting, and dissemination of results under subsections (a), (c), (d), and (f),<ns0:ref class="footnoteRef" idref="fn003925">1</ns0:ref><ns0:note type="footnote" id="fn003925"><ns0:num>1</ns0:num> See References in Text note below.</ns0:note> the Secretary is authorized to reserve up to 2 percent of the amounts appropriated pursuant to subparagraphs (1) and (2) for administration of the program as well as for planning and technical assistance.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>

<ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I21" class="indent0">Subsec. (f) of this section, which required the Secretary to submit to the Committee on Education and Labor of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Labor and Human Resources of the Senate an annual report describing programs for which grants were made under this section in the most recently completed fiscal year and the evaluations received under subsec. (a)(1)(D) of this section in such fiscal year, describing the methods used by the Secretary to comply with subsec. </ns0:note>

<ns0:section style="-uslm-lc:I80" id="id9c08dbf8-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926"><ns0:num value="9926">§ 9926.</ns0:num><ns0:heading> Projects to expand the number of job opportunities available to certain low-income individuals</ns0:heading><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbf9-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/a"><ns0:num value="a" class="bold">(a)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">The Secretary of Health and Human Services (in this section referred to as the “Secretary”) shall enter into agreements with nonprofit organizations (including community development corporations) submitting applications under this section for the purpose of conducting projects in accordance with subsection (b) to create employment opportunities for certain low-income individuals.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbfa-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/b"><ns0:num value="b" class="bold">(b)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Nature of project</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbfb-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/b/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:content> Each nonprofit organization conducting a project under this section shall provide technical and financial assistance to private employers in the community to assist them in creating employment and business opportunities for those individuals eligible to participate in the projects as described in this subsection.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbfc-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/b/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> For purposes of this section, a nonprofit organization is any organization (including a community development corporation) exempt from taxation under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t26/s501/a">section 501(a) of title 26</ns0:ref> by reason of paragraph (3) or (4) of section 501(c) of such title.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbfd-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/b/3"><ns0:num value="3">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:content> A low-income individual eligible to participate in a project conducted under this section is any individual eligible to receive assistance under the program funded part <ns0:ref class="footnoteRef" idref="fn003926">1</ns0:ref><ns0:note type="footnote" id="fn003926"><ns0:num>1</ns0:num> So in original. Probably should be “under part”.</ns0:note> A of title IV of the Social Security Act [<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s601">42 U.S.C. 601</ns0:ref> et seq.] of the State in which the individual resides and any other individual whose income level does not exceed 100 percent of the official poverty line as defined by the Office of Management and Budget and revised in accordance with <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s9902/2">section 9902(2) of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dbfe-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c"><ns0:num value="c" class="bold">(c)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Content of applications; selection priority</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dbff-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c/1"><ns0:num value="1">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> Each nonprofit organization submitting an application under this section shall, as part of such application, describe—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dc00-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c/1/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the technical and financial assistance that will be made available under the project conducted under this section;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dc01-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c/1/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the geographic area to be served by the project;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dc02-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c/1/C"><ns0:num value="C">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the percentage of low-income individuals (as described in subsection (b)) and individuals receiving assistance under a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s601">42 U.S.C. 601</ns0:ref> et seq.] in the area to be served by the project; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1" id="id9c08dc03-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c/1/D"><ns0:num value="D">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:content> unemployment rates in the geographic areas to be served and (to the extent practicable) the jobs available and skills necessary to fill those vacancies in such areas.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0" id="id9c08dc04-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/c/2"><ns0:num value="2">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:content> In approving applications under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to applications proposing to serve those areas containing the highest percentage of individuals receiving assistance under a State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s601">42 U.S.C. 601</ns0:ref> et seq.].</ns0:content>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dc05-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/d"><ns0:num value="d" class="bold">(d)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Administration</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">Each nonprofit organization participating in a project conducted under this section shall provide assurances in its agreement with the Secretary that it has or will have a cooperative relationship with the agency responsible for administering the the <ns0:ref class="footnoteRef" idref="fn003927">2</ns0:ref><ns0:note type="footnote" id="fn003927"><ns0:num>2</ns0:num> So in original.</ns0:note> State program funded under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act [<ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t42/s601">42 U.S.C. 601</ns0:ref> et seq.] in the area served by the project.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>
<ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id9c08dc06-86b3-11f1-9949-c831ab2bbedc" identifier="/us/usc/t42/s9926/e"><ns0:num value="e" class="bold">(e)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Authorization of appropriations</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I11" class="indent0">For the purpose of conducting projects under this section, there is authorized to be appropriated an amount not to exceed $25,000,000 for any fiscal year.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subsection>

accepted.summary: The purposes of chapter 106 are to provide assistance to States and local communities, working through a network of community action agencies and other neighborhood-based organizations, for the reduction of poverty, the revitalization of low-income communities, and the empowerment of low-income families and individuals in rural and urban areas to become fully self-sufficient (particularly families who are attempting to transition off a State program carried out under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.)).
accepted.quote:
The purposes of this chapter are—

(1) to provide assistance to States and local communities, working through a network of community action agencies and other neighborhood-based organizations, for the reduction of poverty, the revitalization of low-income communities, and the empowerment of low-income families and individuals in rural and urban areas to become fully self-sufficient (particularly families who are attempting to transition off a State program carried out under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.)); and

evidence.quote: The purposes of this chapter are—

(1) to provide assistance to States and local communities, working through a network of community action agencies and other neighborhood-based organizations, for the reduction of poverty, the revitalization of low-income communities, and the empowerment of low-income families and individuals in rural and urban areas to become fully self-sufficient (particularly families who are attempting to transition off a State program carried out under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.)); and

accepted.summary: The purposes of chapter 106 include accomplishing the reduction of poverty, revitalization of low-income communities, and empowerment goals through: (A) strengthening community capabilities for planning and coordinating the use of a broad range of Federal, State, local, and other assistance (including private resources) related to the elimination of poverty, so that assistance can be used in a manner responsive to local needs and conditions; (B) organizing a range of services related to the needs of low-income families and individuals, so that these services may have a measurable and potentially major impact on the causes of poverty in the community and may help the families and individuals achieve self-sufficiency; (C) greater use of innovative and effective community-based approaches to attacking the causes and effects of poverty and community breakdown; (D) maximum participation of residents of the low-income communities and members of the groups served by programs assisted through the block grants to empower them to respond to unique problems and needs within their communities; and (E) broadening the resource base of programs directed to the elimination of poverty to secure a more active role in the provision of services for private, religious, charitable, and neighborhood-based organizations, as well as individual citizens, and business, labor, and professional groups able to influence the quantity and quality of opportunities and services for the poor.

evidence.quote: (2) to accomplish the goals described in paragraph (1) through—

(i) private, religious, charitable, and neighborhood-based organizations; and

(ii) individual citizens, and business, labor, and professional groups, who are able to influence the quantity and quality of opportunities and services for the poor.

accepted.summary: Under Executive Order No. 13969, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall take steps, consistent with law, to allow funds available through the Community Services Block Grant program to be used by grantees and eligible entities to provide emergency learning scholarships to disadvantaged families for use by any child without access to in-person learning, which scholarships may be used for: (i) tuition and fees for a private or parochial school; (ii) homeschool, microschool, or learning-pod costs; (iii) special education and related services, including therapies; or (iv) tutoring or remedial education.

evidence.quote: Sec. 2. Providing Emergency Learning Scholarships for Students. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall take steps, consistent with law, to allow funds available through the Community Services Block Grant program to be used by grantees and eligible entities to provide emergency learning scholarships to disadvantaged families for use by any child without access to in-person learning. These scholarships may be used for:
(i) tuition and fees for a private or parochial school;
(ii) homeschool, microschool, or learning-pod costs;
(iii) special education and related services, including therapies; or
(iv) tutoring or remedial education.

accepted.summary: In chapter 106, "poverty line" means the official poverty line defined by the Office of Management and Budget based on the most recent data available from the Bureau of the Census.

defined_terms.label: poverty line
defined_terms.quote: The term “poverty line” means the official poverty line defined by the Office of Management and Budget based on the most recent data available from the Bureau of the Census. The Secretary shall revise annually (or at any shorter interval the Secretary determines to be feasible and desirable) the poverty line, which shall be used as a criterion of eligibility in the community services block grant program established under this chapter. The required revision shall be accomplished by multiplying the official poverty line by the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the annual or other interval immediately preceding the time at which the revision is made. Whenever a State determines that it serves the objectives of the block grant program established under this chapter, the State may revise the poverty line to not to exceed 125 percent of the official poverty line otherwise applicable under this paragraph.

accepted.summary: The members of the tripartite board referred to in paragraph (1) must be selected by the entity and the board must be composed so as to assure that: (A) ⅓ of the members of the board are elected public officials, holding office on the date of selection, or their representatives, except that if the number of such elected officials reasonably available and willing to serve on the board is less than ⅓ of the membership of the board, membership on the board of appointive public officials or their representatives may be counted in meeting such ⅓ requirement; (B)(i) not fewer than ⅓ of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that these members are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served; and (ii) each representative of low-income individuals and families selected to represent a specific neighborhood within a community under clause (i) resides in the neighborhood represented by the member; and (C) the remainder of the members are officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, law enforcement, education, or other major groups and interests in the community served.

accepted.summary: If the State determines, on the basis of a final decision in a review pursuant to section 9914 of this title, that an eligible entity fails to comply with the terms of an agreement, or the State plan, to provide services under this chapter or to meet appropriate standards, goals, and other requirements established by the State (including performance objectives), the State must: (1) inform the entity of the deficiency to be corrected; (2) require the entity to correct the deficiency; (3)(A) offer training and technical assistance, if appropriate, to help correct the deficiency, and prepare and submit to the Secretary a report describing the training and technical assistance offered, or (B) if the State determines that such training and technical assistance are not appropriate, prepare and submit to the Secretary a report stating the reasons for the determination; (4)(A) at the discretion of the State (taking into account the seriousness of the deficiency and the time reasonably required to correct the deficiency), allow the entity to develop and implement, within 60 days after being informed of the deficiency, a quality improvement plan to correct such deficiency within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the State, and (B) not later than 30 days after receiving from an eligible entity a proposed quality improvement plan pursuant to subparagraph (A), either approve such proposed plan or specify the reasons why the proposed plan cannot be approved; and (5) after providing adequate notice and an opportunity for a hearing, initiate proceedings to terminate the designation of or reduce the funding under this chapter of the eligible entity unless the entity corrects the deficiency.

accepted.scope_text: At the end of each fiscal year beginning after September 30, 1999
accepted.summary: At the end of each fiscal year beginning after September 30, 1999, the Secretary shall, directly or by grant or contract, prepare a report containing: (A) a summary of the planned use of funds by each State, and the eligible entities in the State, under the community services block grant program, as contained in each State plan submitted pursuant to section 9908 of this title; (B) a description of how funds were actually spent by the State and eligible entities in the State, including a breakdown of funds spent on administrative costs and on the direct delivery of local services by eligible entities; (C) information on the number of entities eligible for funds under this chapter, the number of low-income persons served under this chapter, and such demographic data on the low-income populations served by eligible entities as is determined by the Secretary to be feasible; (D) a comparison of the planned uses of funds for each State and the actual uses of the funds; (E) a summary of each State’s performance results, and the results for the eligible entities, as collected and submitted by the States in accordance with subsection (a)(2); and (F) any additional information that the Secretary considers to be appropriate to carry out this chapter, if the Secretary informs the States of the need for such additional information and allows a reasonable period of time for the States to collect and provide the information.

accepted.summary: For any program carried out by the Federal Government, or by a State or local government under this chapter, the government shall consider, on the same basis as other nongovernmental organizations, religious organizations to provide the assistance under the program, so long as the program is implemented in a manner consistent with the Establishment Clause of the first amendment to the Constitution.

accepted.summary: Any instructional activity carried out by an eligible service provider receiving a grant under 42 U.S.C. 9923 must be carried out on the campus of an institution of higher education (as defined in section 1141(a) of title 20) and must include: access to the facilities and resources of such an institution; an initial medical examination and follow-up referral or treatment, without charge, for youth during their participation in such activity; at least one nutritious meal daily, without charge, for participating youth during each day of participation; high quality instruction in a variety of sports (which must include swimming and may include dance and any other high quality recreational activity) provided by coaches and teachers from institutions of higher education and from elementary and secondary schools (as defined in section 7801 of title 20); and enrichment instruction and information on matters relating to the well-being of youth, including educational opportunities and information on study practices, education for the prevention of drug and alcohol abuse, and information on health and nutrition, career opportunities, and family and job responsibilities.

rkaf:assertsValue.@value: The purposes of chapter 106 include accomplishing the reduction of poverty, revitalization of low-income communities, and empowerment goals through: (A) strengthening community capabilities for planning and coordinating the use of a broad range of Federal, State, local, and other assistance (including private resources) related to the elimination of poverty, so that assistance can be used in a manner responsive to local needs and conditions; (B) organizing a range of services related to the needs of low-income families and individuals, so that these services may have a measurable and potentially major impact on the causes of poverty in the community and may help the families and individuals achieve self-sufficiency; (C) greater use of innovative and effective community-based approaches to attacking the causes and effects of poverty and community breakdown; (D) maximum participation of residents of the low-income communities and members of the groups served by programs assisted through the block grants to empower them to respond to unique problems and needs within their communities; and (E) broadening the resource base of programs directed to the elimination of poverty to secure a more active role in the provision of services for private, religious, charitable, and neighborhood-based organizations, as well as individual citizens, and business, labor, and professional groups able to influence the quantity and quality of opportunities and services for the poor.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: Sec. 2. Providing Emergency Learning Scholarships for Students. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall take steps, consistent with law, to allow funds available through the Community Services Block Grant program to be used by grantees and eligible entities to provide emergency learning scholarships to disadvantaged families for use by any child without access to in-person learning. These scholarships may be used for:
(i) tuition and fees for a private or parochial school;
(ii) homeschool, microschool, or learning-pod costs;
(iii) special education and related services, including therapies; or
(iv) tutoring or remedial education.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (A) Eligible entity
The term “eligible entity” means an entity—

(i) that is an eligible entity described in paragraph (1) (as in effect on the day before October 27, 1998) as of the day before October 27, 1998, or is designated by the process described in section 9909 of this title (including an organization serving migrant or seasonal farmworkers that is so described or designated); and

(ii) that has a tripartite board or other mechanism described in subsection (a) or (b), as appropriate, of section 9910 of this title.
In this chapter:

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: The term “poverty line” means the official poverty line defined by the Office of Management and Budget based on the most recent data available from the Bureau of the Census. The Secretary shall revise annually (or at any shorter interval the Secretary determines to be feasible and desirable) the poverty line, which shall be used as a criterion of eligibility in the community services block grant program established under this chapter. The required revision shall be accomplished by multiplying the official poverty line by the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the annual or other interval immediately preceding the time at which the revision is made. Whenever a State determines that it serves the objectives of the block grant program established under this chapter, the State may revise the poverty line to not to exceed 125 percent of the official poverty line otherwise applicable under this paragraph.

(2) 1½ percent for activities authorized in sections 9913 through 9918 of this title, of which—

(A) not less than ½ of the amount reserved by the Secretary under this paragraph shall be distributed directly to eligible entities, organizations, or associations described in section 9913(c)(2) of this title for the purpose of carrying out activities described in section 9913(c) of this title; and

(B) ½ of the remainder of the amount reserved by the Secretary under this paragraph shall be used by the Secretary to carry out evaluation and to assist States in carrying out corrective action activities and monitoring (to correct programmatic deficiencies of eligible entities), as described in sections 9914(c) and 9913 of this title; and

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (a) Allotments in general

The Secretary shall, from the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of this title for each fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in section 9903(b) of this title, allot to each State (subject to section 9911 of this title) an amount that bears the same ratio to such remaining amount as the amount received by the State for fiscal year 1981 under section 2808 1
1 See References in Text note below.
of this title bore to the total amount received by all States for fiscal year 1981 under such section, except—

(1) that no State shall receive less than ¼ of 1 percent of the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of this title for such fiscal year; and

(2) as provided in subsection (b).

(1) Minimum allotments

Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), if the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of this title for a fiscal year that remains after the Secretary makes the reservations required in section 9903(b) of this title exceeds $345,000,000, the Secretary shall allot to each State not less than ½ of 1 percent of the amount appropriated under section 9903(a) of this title for such fiscal year.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (1) Use of remainder

If a State uses less than 100 percent of the grant or allotment received under section 9905 or 9906 of this title to make grants under subsection (a), the State shall use the remainder of the grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title (subject to paragraph (2)) for activities that may include—

@graph.rkaf:applicabilityCondition: If a State uses less than 100 percent of the grant or allotment received under section 9905 or 9906 to make grants under subsection (a), subject to paragraph (2)

rkaf:assertsValue.@value: If a State uses less than 100 percent of the grant or allotment received under section 9905 or 9906 of this title to make grants under subsection (a), the State shall use the remainder of the grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title (subject to paragraph (2)) for activities that may include providing training and technical assistance to entities in need; coordinating State-operated and optional locally-operated programs and services targeted to low-income children and families with services provided by eligible entities and other funded organizations, including detailing appropriate employees to ensure increased access; supporting statewide coordination and communication among eligible entities; analyzing fund distribution to determine targeting to areas of greatest need; supporting asset-building programs for low-income individuals; supporting innovative programs and activities conducted by community action agencies or other neighborhood-based organizations; supporting State charity tax credits as described in subsection (c); and supporting other activities consistent with the purposes of this chapter.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: No State may spend more than the greater of $55,000, or 5 percent, of the grant received under section 9905 of this title or State allotment received under section 9906 of this title for administrative expenses, including monitoring activities. Funds to be spent for such expenses shall be taken from the portion of the grant under section 9905 of this title or State allotment that remains after the State makes grants to eligible entities under subsection (a). The cost of activities conducted under paragraph (1)(A) shall not be considered to be administrative expenses. The startup cost and cost of administrative activities conducted under subsection (c) shall be considered to be administrative expenses.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (i) In general
The term “qualified charity” means any organization—
(I) that is—
(B) Qualified charity

rkaf:assertsValue.@value: The term “qualified charity” means any organization that is described in section 501(c)(3) of title 26 and exempt from tax under section 501(a) of such title, an eligible entity, or a public housing agency as defined in section 1437a(b)(6) of this title; that is certified by the appropriate State authority as meeting the requirements of clauses (iii) and (iv); and if such organization is otherwise required to file a return under section 6033 of title 26, that elects to treat the information required to be furnished by clause (v) as being specified in section 6033(b) of such title.

The term “poverty program expense” means any expense in providing direct services referred to in clause (iii).


(bb) Exceptions

Such term shall not include any management or general expense, any expense for the purpose of influencing legislation (as defined in section 4911(d) of title 26), any expense for the purpose of fundraising, any expense for a legal service provided on behalf of any individual referred to in clause (iii), any expense for providing tuition assistance relating to compulsory school attendance, and any expense that consists of a payment to an affiliate of the organization.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (v) Reporting requirement
The information required to be furnished under this clause about an organization is—

(I) the percentages determined by dividing the following categories of the organization’s expenses for the year by the total expenses of the organization for the year: expenses for direct services, management expenses, general expenses, fundraising expenses, and payments to affiliates; and

(II) the category or categories (including food, shelter, education, substance abuse prevention or treatment, job training, or other) of services that constitute predominant activities of the organization.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (vi) Additional requirements for collection organizations
The requirements of this clause are met if the organization—

(I) maintains separate accounting for revenues and expenses; and

(II) makes available to the public information on the administrative and fundraising costs of the organization, and information as to the organizations receiving funds from the organization and the amount of such funds.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (vii) Special rule for States requiring tax uniformity
In the case of a State—

(I) that has a constitutional requirement of tax uniformity; and

(II) that, as of December 31, 1997, imposed a tax on personal income with—
shall be treated

(aa) a single flat rate applicable to all earned and unearned income (except insofar as any amount is not taxed pursuant to tax forgiveness provisions); and

(bb) no generally available exemptions or deductions to individuals;

@graph.rkaf:applicabilityCondition: In the case of a State with a constitutional requirement of tax uniformity and meeting specified December 31, 1997 personal income tax conditions

rkaf:assertsValue.@value: In the case of a State that has a constitutional requirement of tax uniformity and that, as of December 31, 1997, imposed a tax on personal income with a single flat rate applicable to all earned and unearned income (except insofar as any amount is not taxed pursuant to tax forgiveness provisions) and no generally available exemptions or deductions to individuals, the requirement of paragraph (2) shall be treated as met if the amount of the credit described in paragraph (2) is limited to a uniform percentage (but not greater than 25 percent) of State personal income tax liability (determined without regard to credits).

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (b) State application and plan

Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, a State shall prepare and submit to the Secretary an application and State plan covering a period of not less than 1 fiscal year and not more than 2 fiscal years. The plan shall be submitted not later than 30 days prior to the beginning of the first fiscal year covered by the plan, and shall contain such information as the Secretary shall require, including—
(1) an assurance that funds made available through the grant or allotment will be used—

(A) to support activities that are designed to assist low-income families and individuals, including families and individuals receiving assistance under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 601 et seq.), homeless families and individuals, migrant or seasonal farmworkers, and elderly low-income individuals and families, and a description of how such activities will enable the families and individuals—

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (c) Funding termination or reductions
For purposes of making a determination in accordance with subsection (b)(8) with respect to—
(1) a funding reduction, the term “cause” includes—
(A) a statewide redistribution of funds provided through a community services block grant under this chapter to respond to—

(i) the results of the most recently available census or other appropriate data;

(ii) the designation of a new eligible entity; or

(iii) severe economic dislocation; or


(B) the failure of an eligible entity to comply with the terms of an agreement or a State plan, or to meet a State requirement, as described in section 9915(a) of this title; and

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (1) In general

If any geographic area of a State is not, or ceases to be, served by an eligible entity under this chapter, and if the chief executive officer of the State decides to serve such area, the chief executive officer may solicit applications from, and designate as an eligible entity—

(A) a private nonprofit organization (which may include an eligible entity) that is geographically located in the unserved area, that is capable of providing a broad range of services designed to eliminate poverty and foster self-sufficiency, and that meets the requirements of this chapter; and

(B) a private nonprofit eligible entity that is geographically located in an area contiguous to or within reasonable proximity of the unserved area and that is already providing related services in the unserved area.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (2) Selection and composition of board
The members of the board referred to in paragraph (1) shall be selected by the entity and the board shall be composed so as to assure that—

(A) ⅓ of the members of the board are elected public officials, holding office on the date of selection, or their representatives, except that if the number of such elected officials reasonably available and willing to serve on the board is less than ⅓ of the membership of the board, membership on the board of appointive public officials or their representatives may be counted in meeting such ⅓ requirement;

(B)

(i) not fewer than ⅓ of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that these members are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served; and

(ii) each representative of low-income individuals and families selected to represent a specific neighborhood within a community under clause (i) resides in the neighborhood represented by the member; and


(C) the remainder of the members are officials or members of business, industry, labor, religious, law enforcement, education, or other major groups and interests in the community served.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (b) Public organizations

In order for a public organization to be considered to be an eligible entity for purposes of section 9902(1) of this title, the entity shall administer the community services block grant program through—

(1) a tripartite board, which shall have members selected by the organization and shall be composed so as to assure that not fewer than ⅓ of the members are persons chosen in accordance with democratic selection procedures adequate to assure that these members—

(A) are representative of low-income individuals and families in the neighborhood served;

(B) reside in the neighborhood served; and

(C) are able to participate actively in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs funded under this chapter; or


(2) another mechanism specified by the State to assure decisionmaking and participation by low-income individuals in the development, planning, implementation, and evaluation of programs funded under this chapter.

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (a) Reservation
If, with respect to any State, the Secretary—

(1) receives a request from the governing body of an Indian tribe or tribal organization within the State that assistance under this chapter be made directly to such tribe or organization; and

(2) determines that the members of such tribe or tribal organization would be better served by means of grants made directly to provide benefits under this chapter,


the Secretary shall reserve from amounts that would otherwise be allotted to such State under section 9906 of this title for the fiscal year the amount determined under subsection (b).
